runtime-info.title: Runtime metrics guide
runtime-info.subtitle: What every number on a runtime card actually means
runtime-info.intro: Each card shows a live snapshot of a single <highlight>Umiji process</highlight>. Use this guide to understand what each metric measures and when to worry about it.
runtime-info.instance-types-description: Umiji is split into several specialized processes. Each one has its own job, its own memory, and its own event loop.
runtime-info.api-description: Handles every HTTP request from the dashboard and subscription endpoints. This is the <highlight>main user-facing process</highlight> — virtually every panel and subscription request is served here.
runtime-info.scheduler-description: A <highlight>cron-driven dispatcher</highlight>. It does not run any work itself — at the scheduled moment it simply pushes a job into the queue for the <highlight>Processor</highlight> to pick up.
runtime-info.processor-description: The actual <highlight>worker</highlight>. It consumes queued jobs and runs the heavy lifting: <highlight>node health checks</highlight>, <highlight>traffic aggregation</highlight> per user and per node, and other long-running tasks that must not block the API.
runtime-info.memory-description: Where the process holds its working data. All values are reported by Node.js in real time.
runtime-info.heap-description: Memory used by JavaScript objects, managed by <highlight>V8</highlight> — the Node.js engine. Shown as <highlight>used / total</highlight>. A high ratio is <highlight>expected and healthy</highlight> — V8 holds onto memory until it really needs more, so something like <highlight>100 / 120 MB</highlight> is normal, not a warning.
runtime-info.rss-description: <highlight>Resident Set Size</highlight> — the total physical memory the OS has given to the process, including the heap, native code, and shared libraries. The best single signal of <highlight>how much RAM this process is actually using</highlight>.
runtime-info.external-description: Memory held outside V8 by native C++ objects bound to JavaScript — typical sources are <highlight>open sockets</highlight>, <highlight>streams</highlight>, and Buffer-backed payloads.
runtime-info.array-buffers-description: Memory specifically allocated for <highlight>ArrayBuffer</highlight> and <highlight>Buffer</highlight> instances (raw binary data). It is counted as a subset of <highlight>External</highlight>.
runtime-info.event-loop-description: Health of the single-threaded loop that drives all asynchronous work in Node.js. If the loop is blocked, the whole process stalls.
runtime-info.delay-description: Average time between consecutive event loop ticks. A healthy value sits close to <highlight>0–2 ms</highlight>. Higher numbers mean the loop is being blocked by long synchronous work.
runtime-info.p99-description: <highlight>99th percentile</highlight> of event loop delay over the measurement window. Reveals worst-case latency that the average alone hides — useful for spotting occasional spikes.
runtime-info.active-handles-description: Long-lived resources keeping the loop alive: <highlight>open sockets</highlight>, <highlight>timers</highlight>, <highlight>file descriptors</highlight>. A steady state is normal; <highlight>unbounded growth</highlight> is a strong leak signal.

info.title: How usage is calculated
info.summary: Returns internal squad members who spent at least the given threshold over the selected period, with the total volume for each of them.
info.nodes-intro: A squad isn't tied to nodes directly — the link is derived through inbounds:
info.nodes-step-1: All inbounds that belong to the internal squad are taken.
info.nodes-step-2: For each inbound, the config profiles it belongs to are resolved.
info.nodes-step-3: A node is counted when it has such a profile set as active and that inbound is enabled on the node itself.
info.nodes-outro: So only the nodes a squad member can <hl>actually connect to right now</hl> are counted. If the squad has no inbound available on at least one node, the list is empty.
info.traffic-granularity: Stats are stored with daily granularity: one record = user + node + day. Node data is flushed to the database roughly every 2 minutes, so today's numbers are near real-time, lagging by up to a couple of minutes.
info.traffic-sum: For each member, all of their daily per-node records are summed over the period from the start of start to the end of end (both dates inclusive, UTC).
info.traffic-threshold: Only users whose total is ≥ minTotalBytes make it into the response. Volume is returned in raw bytes, without rounding.
info.caveats-per-node: Traffic is counted per whole node, not per inbound. If a node is shared across squads (its active profile also serves other inbounds), the user's total includes all their traffic on that node — including what they poured through other squads' inbounds. It's an upper bound, not exact per-squad attribution.
info.caveats-membership: Squad membership and the node set are taken at request time, not historically. A user who left the squad disappears from the response (even though they used traffic); a recently joined one shows all their traffic for the period, including days before joining. The same goes for a change of a node's active profile.
info.caveats-sorting: The list is sorted by user ID, not by volume. Since traffic changes in real time, data may drift between pages — to hunt down abusers, set a minTotalBytes threshold instead of reading everyone.

node-ssh.import-description: Restores keys from a backup file. Enter the recovery phrase that the backup was created with.
node-ssh.import-invalid: This file is not a vault backup
node-ssh.import-mismatch: The recovery phrase does not open this backup
node-ssh.reset-description: Deletes the vault and every SSH key in it. The private keys are gone for good, so the public keys already installed on your nodes become useless and you will have to install a new one on each. Panel access is not affected.
node-ssh.lost-everything: Lost both the passcode and the phrase?

brokers.page-description: Accounts that sell your service. Each broker manages only its own users, within the limits you set.
brokers.no-brokers-description: Create a broker to let a reseller manage their own users from this panel.
brokers.username-description: Used to sign in. It must be unique across the panel.
brokers.password-description: At least 24 characters with uppercase and lowercase letters and numbers.
brokers.new-password-description: Leave empty to keep the current password.
brokers.traffic-quota-description: Total traffic all users of this broker can use. 0 means unlimited.
brokers.users-limit-description: Maximum number of users the broker can own. Leave empty for unlimited.
brokers.expire-at-description: After this date the broker can still sign in and look around, but can't change anything, and all of its users expire.
brokers.internal-squads-description: Internal squads the broker can assign to its users.
brokers.account-enabled-description: A disabled broker cannot sign in. Their users keep working.
brokers.reset-usage-description: Set the used traffic of {{username}} back to zero. Users limited by the quota become active again.
brokers.delete-description: Delete {{username}}? Their users stay in the panel and become yours.
brokers.quota-exhausted-alert: Your traffic quota is used up, so your users are paused. Contact the panel owner to extend it.
brokers.external-squad-description: Each broker gets its own external squad and subscription page, named after it. Its users always use them. The broker can brand both; templates, hosts and HWID stay with you.

panel.status-expired-hint: Read-only until the owner extends it.
panel.status-exhausted-hint: Your users are paused until the quota is raised.
panel.expired-alert: You can still look around, but you can't make changes. Your users are paused until the panel owner extends your account.

broker-bot.title: Telegram Bot
broker-bot.description: Sell your plans through your own Telegram bot. Customers top up a wallet, then buy a plan in one tap.

stats.title: Bot stats
stats.description: Customers, sales, top-ups, free trials and referrals of your bot. Days are UTC.
stats.reset-note: Counted since you last changed the bot token. Receipts waiting are all of them.

connection.title: Bot connection
connection.help: Create a bot with @BotFather, make a group with Topics enabled, add the bot to it as an admin (with Manage Topics), then paste the bot token here. You can leave the group ID empty and find it with the Group ID Finder.
connection.topics-missing: Topics not created. Check the group
connection.bot-token-keep: Leave empty to keep the current token
connection.group-id-hint: Leave empty if you don't know it and use the Group ID Finder.
connection.disconnect-confirm: Disconnect the bot? Customers can't use it until you connect it again. Plans, payment methods, customers and their wallets are kept.

finder.title: Group ID Finder
finder.help: Pick the staff group without looking up its ID: the bot lists every group you send /find in.
finder.step-connect: Connect your bot in Bot connection
finder.step-add: Add the bot to your staff group as an admin
finder.step-find: Send /find in the group, then refresh here

channel.title: Channel
channel.description: A public channel link, shown as an “Our channel” button next to Support on the bot's start menu.
channel.url-hint: Leave empty to hide the button.

topup.title: Top up a customer
topup.description: Credit a customer's wallet by their Telegram numeric ID. They must have started the bot.
topup.invalid-id: Enter a valid Telegram numeric ID (digits only).
topup.invalid-amount: Enter a valid amount in Toman.

plans.title: Plans
plans.description: What customers can buy in your bot.
plans.help-1: A plan is a package customers buy in your bot: a traffic limit, a duration, the internal squad it runs on and the price in Toman. Traffic 0 means unlimited.
plans.help-2: Customers pay from their bot wallet, so they top it up first. You approve the top-up receipts here or in the staff group.
plans.help-3: Every subscription sold is one of your users: it counts toward your users limit and its traffic counts toward your traffic quota.
plans.help-4: Avoid unlimited plans unless your quota allows it: the customer's usage is uncapped and all of it comes out of your quota.
plans.help-5: Sales pause on their own while your account is disabled, expired, out of quota or at its users limit. Pause a plan to stop selling it without deleting it.
plans.field-squads-hint: Each subscription sold from this plan gets every squad you tick.
plans.no-squads: No internal squads are available to you yet. Ask the panel owner to allow one.
plans.delete-confirm: Delete this plan? Customers won't see it anymore. Subscriptions already sold are not affected.
plans.field-ip-limit-hint: How many IPs each buyer can connect from at the same time, across all nodes. Devices on one Wi‑Fi count once. Empty = unlimited. This is a beta and doesn’t always work.

categories.title: Plan categories
categories.hint: Group plans into sections in the bot's buy menu. Optional.
categories.empty: No categories yet. Plans without a category show directly in the bot.
categories.delete-confirm: Delete this category? Its plans stay, just without a category.

payments.title: Payment methods
payments.description: Shown to customers when they top up their wallet. Add at least one.
payments.no-other: No other methods yet. PayPal, Wise, IBAN, SBP, YooMoney and the like go here.

channels.title: Mandatory channels
channels.description: Customers must join these before they can use the bot. The bot must be an admin of each channel: if it can't check membership, it lets everyone through.
channels.label: Button label
channels.ref-invalid: Must be a @username or a -100… numeric ID

orders.title: Orders
orders.description: Wallet top-ups to review and everything your bot has sold.
orders.receipt-in-telegram: The receipt was sent in Telegram.
orders.recover-user-hint: Enter the user ID created for this purchase. It must belong to this broker and match the customer's Telegram account.
orders.refund-purchase-confirm: No matching subscription was found. Refund {{amount}} to this customer's wallet?
orders.approve-confirm: Approve this top-up? {{amount}} goes to the customer's wallet and they're notified.
orders.reject-confirm: Reject this top-up? The customer is notified and no balance is added.
orders.connect-first: Connect your bot to review receipts.

broker-bot.broadcast-notice: 📣 Heads up: every now and then we may share a platform announcement or promotion with your bot’s subscribers. Nothing spammy, just the occasional update. Thanks for being part of the platform! 💜

broadcast.title: Bot Broadcast
broadcast.description: Send a message to every customer of every broker’s bot.
broadcast.audience_one: Goes to {{count}} customer of the connected broker bots.
broadcast.audience_other: Goes to {{count}} customers of the connected broker bots.
broadcast.image-hint: Optional. JPG/PNG up to 10 MB, sent with the message as a photo (the message then fits 1024 characters).
broadcast.confirm_one: Send this to {{count}} customer now? It can't be undone.
broadcast.confirm_other: Send this to {{count}} customers now? It can't be undone.
broadcast.recent-description: Delivery runs in the background through each broker’s own bot.
broadcast.error-empty: Add a message or an image.

referral.title: Referral program
referral.description: Every customer gets a personal invite link under “🤝 Invite friends”. When a friend who first opened the bot through that link gets a top-up approved, the customer who invited them gets a share of it as wallet credit. Only the inviter is paid, never the person who invited them.
referral.percent-hint: 0 turns the program off and hides the button. Wallet credit you add from this panel pays no reward.

trial.title: Free trial
trial.description: A free test plan every Telegram account can claim once, under “🎁 Free trial”. Each trial is one of your users, so it counts toward your users limit and traffic quota.
trial.squads-hint: Each free trial gets every squad you tick.
trial.field-ip-limit-hint: How many IPs each trial user can connect from at the same time, across all nodes. Devices on one Wi‑Fi count once. Empty = unlimited. This is a beta and doesn’t always work.
trial.field-daily-limit-hint: The most free trials handed out in one day (UTC). Once they’re gone, customers are told to come back tomorrow. Empty = no cap.
trial.delete-expired-hint: A day after a trial expires, its user is deleted, so it stops counting toward your users limit. Turning this on also deletes trials that expired earlier, and trial users you extended by hand once they expire again.
trial.reset-confirm: Let every Telegram account claim the free trial again? Trials already handed out keep working.

broker-bot-texts.description: Write what your bot says, in every language it speaks. Saved changes reach customers right away.

languages.title: Languages
languages.description: Customers switch between these with the 🌐 button in the menu. A new customer starts in their Telegram app's language when your bot speaks it, otherwise in the default. The staff group always gets the default.
languages.default-locked: The default language stays on. Make another one the default first.

Root-level sections, merged into the **root** of every config that lists this snippet in its root `snippets` array. 


`inbounds`, `api`, `stats` and `metrics` cannot be provided by a snippet.

config-visual-editor.burst-observatory-description: Probes outbounds in bursts, used by leastLoad balancers.
config-visual-editor.managed-root-note: These parts of the Xray config are written by Umiji-node on every start, so anything you put here for them is replaced.

section-description.inbounds: Ports the node listens on. Umiji adds your users to VLESS, Trojan, Shadowsocks, Hysteria and MTProto inbounds.
section-description.outbounds: Where traffic leaves the node. The first one is the default.
section-description.routing: Rules are checked top to bottom. The first match decides the outbound.
section-description.dns: The built-in DNS used for routing and for the DNS outbound.
section-description.log: What Xray writes to its logs.
section-description.observatory: Health checks that feed the balancers.
section-description.fakedns: Fake IP pools handed out for domains, for transparent proxying.
section-description.geodata: Automatic updates for geoip and geosite files.
section-description.advanced: Snippets, environment, version limits and any other top-level keys.

config-visual-editor.choose-protocol: Pick a protocol. You can change every field afterwards.

blurb-in.vless: Light and modern. Pair it with REALITY or XHTTP.
blurb-in.trojan: Password-based, looks like HTTPS. Needs TLS.
blurb-in.hysteria: QUIC-based and fast on lossy links. Needs TLS.
blurb-in.mtproto: Telegram proxy that looks like a normal HTTPS site. Users add it right inside Telegram.
blurb-in.mixed: SOCKS5 and HTTP proxy on one port.
blurb-in.tunnel: Forwards a port to a fixed destination.
blurb-in.tun: Virtual network interface on the node.

blurb-out.freedom: Straight to the internet. Usually tagged DIRECT.
blurb-out.dns: Answers DNS queries with the built-in DNS.
blurb-out.wireguard: Route through a WireGuard peer, like WARP.
blurb-out.loopback: Send traffic back into routing through an inbound.

config-visual-editor.nothing-to-set: This protocol has nothing to set here.
config-visual-editor.broken-json: The JSON has a syntax error
config-visual-editor.broken-json-description: The visual editor needs valid JSON. Fix it in the JSON tab, then come back.

node-install.auto-description: Umiji logs in to the server over SSH, installs Docker and the node, and adds it to the panel for you.
node-install.password-note: Used once to log in over SSH. It is never stored.
node-install.background-note: The installation keeps running. The node shows up in the list when it's ready.

errors.CONNECT_FAILED: Couldn't reach the server over SSH. Check the IP address and SSH port.
errors.AUTH_FAILED: The server rejected the root password.
errors.NOT_ROOT: This login isn't root. The installer needs the root account.
errors.UNSUPPORTED_SYSTEM: This server isn't supported. The node needs Linux on x86_64 or ARM64.
errors.DOCKER_FAILED: Docker couldn't be installed or started. The output below shows why.
errors.CONTAINER_EXISTS: This server already runs an umiji-node container. Remove it first, or use manual setup.
errors.PORT_BUSY: The node port is already in use on this server. Go back and pick another node port.
errors.START_FAILED: The node container couldn't start. The output below shows why.
errors.HANDSHAKE_FAILED: The node is running, but the panel can't reach it. Open the node port in the server's firewall.
errors.REGISTER_FAILED: The node is installed, but adding it to the panel failed.
